purpose: Tepotinib is used to treat a certain type of non-small cell lung cancer in adults. Specifically, it is for lung cancer that has spread and has an abnormal change (mutation) in a gene called MET. Your doctor will test your tumor to confirm this mutation before starting treatment.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have an abnormal MET protein that tells them to keep growing out of control. Tepotinib works like a targeted switch that blocks this faulty MET protein, slowing or stopping the cancer cells from growing and spreading. Because it targets a specific protein, it is more focused than traditional chemotherapy.
common_side_effects: Swelling in your legs, feet, or hands (edema) is the most common side effect. You may also experience nausea, tiredness, shortness of breath, diarrhea, muscle or joint pain, and increased levels of certain liver enzymes on blood tests. Some people notice decreased appetite or constipation.
warnings: Tepotinib can cause serious fluid buildup around the lungs or in the body, which may require dose adjustment or stopping the medicine. It can harm an unborn baby, so use reliable birth control during treatment and for some time after. Tell your doctor right away if you develop sudden worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, or significant swelling. It can also affect liver function, so regular blood tests are needed.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 450 mg (two 225 mg tablets) taken by mouth once a day with food. Try to take it at the same time each day. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush or split them. If you miss a dose and it is more than 8 hours late, skip it and take your next dose as scheduled.
